top-gun-1986.gazette: The Navy opened NAS Miramar and its F-14 crews to the production, and the dogfights were shot from cameras rigged to aircraft actually in the air. Flight time was billed back to the studio, and the service held approval over the script. Recruiting tables went up in theater lobbies that summer.

the-untouchables-1987.gazette: Eliot Ness ran a Prohibition unit against Capone's Chicago, and Capone went down in 1931 for tax evasion, not for anything Ness proved in court. Mamet's script invents Jim Malone outright and stages a rooftop killing that never occurred. The distance between the two accounts has been the film's standing argument ever since.

yeelen-1987.gazette: Cissé staged Bambara ritual on screen, drawing on Komo and Kore practice whose forms the societies that hold them keep closed. Elders and scholars divided over how much had been shown and whether showing it at all broke the terms of the knowledge. The film took the Jury Prize at Cannes in 1987 and carried the dispute abroad with it.
yeelen-1987.prism: Secret knowledge that gets filmed stops being secret and becomes footage, available to anyone with a ticket, on terms its keepers never set. The accuracy question and the disclosure question pull opposite ways here: the more faithful the staging, the more there is to answer for.

a-city-of-sadness-1989.gazette: The 228 Incident of 1947 and the White Terror that followed were closed subjects in Taiwan through nearly four decades of martial law. Hou put the killings and the disappearances on screen two years after that law was lifted, and took the Golden Lion at Venice. The state's own formal apology came six years after the film.

drugstore-cowboy-1989.gazette: James Fogle wrote the source manuscript in prison, out of a career of robbing pharmacies that had run most of his adult life. Van Sant shot in Portland and kept to the book's procedures for 1971: the drugstore scores, the motel rotations, the crew's superstitions about hats and dogs. Two decades after the film opened, Fogle was arrested again for a pharmacy robbery.

the-seventh-continent-1989.gazette: Austrian papers in 1985 carried the case of a family who destroyed everything inside their own apartment and then died there, with no motive ever established. Haneke built the film around the ordinary days preceding it — the meals, the car wash, the bank counter — and declined to supply a cause the reporting did not contain. What the record withheld, the film withholds too.
the-seventh-continent-1989.prism: Refusing to explain is itself a claim about the case: that the ordinary days were the whole of it, and nothing hidden underneath needs finding. That reading is unfalsifiable, which is exactly what makes it land — the film's fidelity to the record doubles as an argument no one can check.

goodfellas-1990.gazette: Henry Hill turned in 1980 and went into witness protection, which is where Nicholas Pileggi found him for Wiseguy. The film runs on that testimony — the Lufthansa haul, the bodies that surfaced after it, the last day counted hour by hour. Hill was eventually expelled from the program for committing crimes while inside it.

a-brighter-summer-day-1991.gazette: In 1961 a Taipei middle-school student stabbed a girl to death near Guling Street; Yang was fourteen in the same city, and the case stayed with him for thirty years. The film sets it among the mainlander families displaced in 1949, living in provisional housing under a state that kept files on them. Its Chinese title names the killing as an incident, in the language of a police report.

boyz-n-the-hood-1991.gazette: Singleton wrote the script about the streets he grew up on and shot it in South Central, on the blocks themselves rather than a backlot. He was twenty-three, and the film's claim was testimony as much as drama: this is the place, filmed where it stands. Violence at opening-night screenings around the country became the story of the release, and studios put guards in the lobbies.
boyz-n-the-hood-1991.prism: A film gets called realistic and then gets held responsible for the reality it filmed — the location shooting that made the testimony credible also made it the thing to point at. Nobody stationed guards outside the pictures shot on a backlot.

center-stage-1991.gazette: Ruan Lingyu killed herself in Shanghai in 1935 at twenty-four, pursued by tabloids that had made her private life a running serial; her funeral pulled crowds into the streets. Kwan cut surviving prints of her films into his own, filmed interviews with people who had worked beside her, and let Maggie Cheung address the camera about playing a woman whose work is mostly lost. The note Ruan left is read aloud in the film, and its authenticity has been argued over ever since.

jungle-fever-1991.gazette: Yusuf Hawkins was sixteen when a crowd of white men in Bensonhurst met him with bats and a gun in August 1989; he had come to Brooklyn to look at a used car. Lee dedicates the film to him in the opening titles and keeps the case inside the frame — the tabloids, the marches, a neighborhood defending itself in public. The picture reached theaters less than two years after the killing.

my-own-private-idaho-1991.gazette: Van Sant put real Portland hustlers on camera in a sequence staged as a rack of magazines, letting them describe the work in their own terms while the actors sat among them. The film's Shakespeare borrowings run alongside that footage without absorbing it. It is the one stretch of the picture where the testimony was not written.
my-own-private-idaho-1991.prism: Real testimony inside a fiction lends the fiction its credibility, and the people who supplied it are not on the residual sheet. The film keeps its Falstaff and its festival prizes; the men keep the interlude.

only-yesterday-1991.gazette: Takahata sent his team to Yamagata to document safflower work: picking before dawn while the dew keeps the thorns soft, then the drying, the pounding, the dye that ends up on someone else's collar. The 1966 passages follow that process step by step instead of summarizing it. Animation researched to that depth was being spent on a twenty-seven-year-old office worker taking her holiday in the countryside.

lessons-of-darkness-1992.gazette: Herzog filmed the Kuwaiti oil fields in 1991 while the wells were still burning, then removed the names — no Iraq, no Kuwait, no war, only a planet and the crews working it. He scored the wreckage to Wagner and Mahler and framed the whole thing as a dispatch from somewhere else. At the Berlin premiere the audience jeered him for aestheticizing an atrocity, and he has defended the method ever since.

farewell-my-concubine-1993.gazette: The opera the film takes its name from is a standing repertory piece, and the dan role Cheng Dieyi trains for demands years of conditioning begun in childhood: voice, footwork, the shape of the hands. Chen put his actors through that training and shot the makeup as a process rather than a cut, brush by brush. The film shared the Palme d'Or in 1993 and was pulled from Chinese screens shortly after its domestic release.
farewell-my-concubine-1993.prism: The training that makes the illusion convincing is the same training the film presents as injury — the beatings in the opera school aren't backdrop to the artistry, they're the method that produced it. Praising the discipline means praising what it cost the boys who were put through it.
